title: multimesh_allocate_data with use_indirect does not initialize command buffer
body:
### Tested versions

4.5 stable

### System information

Godot v4.5.stable - Windows 11 (build 22631) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9159) - AMD Ryzen 5 5500 (12 threads) - 31.87 GiB memory

### Issue description

After calling `multimesh_allocate_data` on a multimesh, the command_buffer is not initialized until the next call to multimesh_set_mesh.
This can be confirmed in current master [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a3e84cc2af14aa4cffbefd8e13492e59567a64e3/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/mesh_storage.cpp#L1580) where the command buffer is reset to null, and only initialized [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a3e84cc2af14aa4cffbefd8e13492e59567a64e3/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/mesh_storage.cpp#L1690) when multimesh_set_mesh is called.

This is understandable when mesh is null, because the command buffer requires information on vertex / index count. However when the mesh is already set, it may be expected for the command buffer to be initialized automatically.

Otherwise, if this is the expected behavior, the docs for [multimesh_allocate_data](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_renderingserver.html#class-renderingserver-method-multimesh-allocate-data) should probably be updated to reflect this information as the current one is empty; while the docs for [multimesh_get_command_buffer_rd_rid](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_renderingserver.html#class-renderingserver-method-multimesh-get-command-buffer-rd-rid) only mentions the following:

> This [RID](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_rid.html#class-rid) is only valid if use_indirect is set to true when allocating data through [multimesh_allocate_data()](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_renderingserver.html#class-renderingserver-method-multimesh-allocate-data)

which could possibly be confusing.




### Steps to reproduce

run the following in a blank scene

```gdscript
extends Node

func _ready() -> void:
	var mm = RenderingServer.multimesh_create()
	var mesh = BoxMesh.new()
	RenderingServer.multimesh_set_mesh(mm, mesh.get_rid())
	RenderingServer.multimesh_allocate_data(mm, 10, RenderingServer.MULTIMESH_TRANSFORM_3D, false, false, true)

	var command_buffer = RenderingServer.multimesh_get_command_buffer_rd_rid(mm)
	print("command buffer: ", command_buffer)
	assert(!command_buffer.is_valid())

	mesh = BoxMesh.new()
	RenderingServer.multimesh_set_mesh(mm, mesh.get_rid())

	command_buffer = RenderingServer.multimesh_get_command_buffer_rd_rid(mm)
	print("command buffer: ", command_buffer)
	assert(command_buffer.is_valid())
```
